glosses: To have turned on (an electronic device).

examples.text: I didn’t hear you because I had the radio on.

glosses: To trick or deceive deliberately; to play a prank on.

examples.text: Near-synonym: have a laugh

glosses: To possess at the point of arrest.

examples.text: I had some pills on me when that cop picked me up.

glosses: To possess evidence of wrongdoing regarding (someone); to press charges on (someone).

examples.text: They have two bodies on me.

glosses: To carry or have equipped on or about one's body, as an item of clothing, equipment, decoration, etc.

glosses: To have or carry on one's person habitually, consistently; or, to maintain in a particular fashion or manner.

examples.text: He wears eyeglasses.
She wears her hair in braids.

glosses: To bear or display in one's aspect or appearance.

examples.text: She wore a smile all day.
He walked out of the courtroom wearing an air of satisfaction.

glosses: To eat away at, erode, diminish, or consume gradually; to cause a gradual deterioration in; to produce (some change) through attrition, exposure, or constant use.

examples.text: You're going to wear a hole in the bottom of those shoes.

Long illness had worn the bloom from her cheeks.
Exile had worn the man to a shadow.

glosses: To undergo gradual deterioration; become impaired; be reduced or consumed gradually due to any continued process, activity, or use.

examples.text: The tiles were wearing thin due to years of children's feet.
His stock of money[…] began to wear very low.
The family that had raised it wore out in the earlier part of this century

glosses: To exhaust, fatigue, expend, or weary.

examples.text: His neverending criticism has finally worn my patience.
Toil and care soon wear the spirit.
Our physical advantage allowed us to wear the other team out and win.

glosses: (in the phrase \"wearing on (someone)\") To cause annoyance, irritation, fatigue, or weariness near the point of an exhaustion of patience.

examples.text: Her high pitched voice is really wearing on me lately.

glosses: To overcome one's reluctance and endure a (previously specified) situation.

examples.text: I know you don't like working with him, but you'll just have to wear it.

glosses: To last or remain durable under hard use or over time; to retain usefulness, value, or desirable qualities under any continued strain or long period of time; sometimes said of a person, regarding the quality of being easy or difficult to tolerate.

examples.text: Don't worry, this fabric will wear. These pants will last you for years.
This color wears so well. I must have washed this sweater a thousand times.
I have to say, our friendship has worn pretty well.
It's hard to get to know him, but he wears well.

glosses: To pass slowly, gradually or tediously.

examples.text: wear on, wear away.
As the years wore on, we seemed to have less and less in common.
Away, I say; time wears.
Thus wore out night.

glosses: To bring (a sailing vessel) onto the other tack by bringing the wind around the stern (as opposed to tacking when the wind is brought around the bow); to come round on another tack by turning away from the wind.
